info.title: Storeshot API
info.description:
The Storeshot public API. Generate App Store and Google Play marketing screenshots.

## Conventions
- JSON fields are camelCase; enum values are lower snake_case; error codes are UPPER_SNAKE.
- Collections are returned as `{ "data": [...] }`.
- Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header. Send your own (1–128 chars of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - =`) to correlate logs.
- Every error uses the `ErrorEnvelope`: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "requestId", "docUrl", "details?" } }`.

Error code reference: `/v1/docs/errors`.

## For AI agents
Start with the agent quickstart (https://storeshot.art/docs/agents-quickstart.md) or https://storeshot.art/llms.txt (every docs page is also Markdown; all of it in one file: https://storeshot.art/llms-full.txt). The usual task, a store listing from raw app screenshots:
1. Read the key from the `STORESHOT_API_KEY` environment variable. If it is missing, stop and ask your human to create a test key (`ss_test_…`, free) in the developer console (https://console.storeshot.art/) and export it. Never print, log or commit a key, and never ask for one in chat.
2. `GET /me` checks the key; `credential.environment` is `test` (free sample images) or `live` (real images, credits).
3. `POST /uploads` once per raw screenshot (PNG, JPEG or WebP).
4. `POST /screenshot-sets?dryRun=true` quotes the set for free. With a live key, tell your human the `credits` before creating it.
5. `POST /screenshot-sets` with an `Idempotency-Key` (a retry never charges twice), then poll `GET /screenshot-sets/{id}` every 3–5 seconds until `status` is no longer `queued` or `running`.
6. `GET /screenshot-sets/{id}/archive?layout=fastlane` and unzip it in the project root (the folders fastlane `deliver` and `supply` read).

**Costs.** A live key spends 1 credit per generated image (a set: screens × devices, +1 for a feature graphic), charged at create and refunded automatically for images that fail or are canceled before they start. Test keys never spend credits. Every other operation is free; each operation ends with its **Credits.** line.

**Asynchronous work.** Creates answer `202` with a `queued` resource: poll it, send `Prefer: wait=60` on generations, or register a webhook. **Errors.** Retry `429` after `Retry-After` and `5xx` with the same `Idempotency-Key`; on `402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` give your human `details.topUpUrl`; quote `X-Request-Id` when asking for help.

## Authentication
Send `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, where the credential is an API key (`ss_live_…` or `ss_test_…`) or a Draggable Auth access token. Never put credentials in the URL. Test keys (`ss_test_…`) never incur charges. Each operation lists the scope an API key needs; access tokens have every scope. No key yet? An agent can get one with the approval of its human: `POST /auth/device`, then poll `POST /auth/device/token` (RFC 8628 device authorization; it may be disabled on a server).

## Client identification
Optionally send `X-Storeshot-Client: <surface>/<name>`, where surface is `api`, `web`, `mcp` or `cli` and name is 1–100 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ @ + -` (for example `cli/storeshot-cli@0.3.1`). It labels your usage (`GET /usage?groupBy=source`); it is not authentication. Without it, usage is labelled `api` and your `User-Agent` is recorded.

## Rate limits
Authenticated requests are counted per minute in two buckets: per API key (`key`, 60 requests) and per account (`user`, 120 requests, shared by all API keys and access tokens of the account; access tokens use only this bucket). Test keys count like live keys. A request is counted only if every bucket allows it; a refused request counts nowhere. The numbers here are the current defaults and may differ per plan: `RateLimit-Policy` is authoritative.

Every authenticated response carries `RateLimit-Policy` (each policy as `"name";q=<requests>;w=<seconds>`) and `RateLimit` (the most restrictive policy as `"name";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds until reset>`), following draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers. Over the limit you get `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` and `details.scope`.

Billed generations are also capped per account: 3 in progress at once (`429 CONCURRENCY_LIMITED`, retry after 10 s) and 100 per UTC day (`429 RATE_LIMITED`, `details.policy` `daily_generations`, retry after the next UTC midnight). `/health`, `/status`, `/devices`, this document and the docs are never rate limited. Browsers can read these headers and `X-Request-Id` (CORS).

## Uploads and retention
Hand an image over once and reference its `id` in generations. Three ways: `POST /uploads` with `multipart/form-data` (one part `file`); `POST /uploads/presign`, then `PUT` the file to the returned URL from your server and call `POST /uploads/{id}/complete`; or `POST /uploads` with `{ "url": "https://…" }` to have the server fetch it. Each way ends in the same `ready` upload with the same metadata.

Accepted: PNG, JPEG and WebP, detected from the bytes (never from the file name or declared type), at most 20 MB and 50 megapixels (16384 pixels per edge). HEIC/HEIF is not supported. An account can hold 500 uploads or 2 GB (pending and ready uploads count; deleting frees space). Test keys may upload too (same limits).

URL imports fetch `https://` URLs on port 443 only, and only from public addresses (private, loopback, link-local and other special-purpose addresses are refused, also after a redirect), with at most 3 redirects and 15 seconds in total. Only the origin and path of the URL are stored.

**Retention:** uploads, with their files, are deleted 30 days after creation (pending or failed uploads after 24 hours); you can delete one earlier with `DELETE /uploads/{id}`. Generated results are kept until you delete them (results of test keys: 30 days).

## Generations
`POST /generations` turns one screenshot into one marketing image of exactly the size a store requires (a `GET /devices` id, or its `width`×`height`). It returns at once with `202` and a generation in `queued`; a worker moves it to `running`, then to `succeeded` (with `result.image.url`), `failed` (with `error.code`) or `canceled`. Retries after a temporary provider error happen inside `running`.

**Waiting.** Poll `GET /generations/{id}` (every 2–5 seconds is plenty), or send `Prefer: wait=<seconds>` (or `?wait=<seconds>`, at most 60) on `POST /generations` or `GET /generations/{id}` to hold the response until the generation is final: `200` when it is, `202` when the time ran out, with `Preference-Applied: wait=<seconds>` when the wait was honoured. A busy server may answer `202` at once without `Preference-Applied`; keep polling then.

**Idempotency.** Send `Idempotency-Key: <1–255 printable ASCII characters>` with every `POST /generations`. Repeating a request with the same key and body returns the original generation (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and never creates or charges a second one; the same key with a different body, or from a credential of the other environment, is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Keys are kept at least as long as the generation exists. A refused request (4xx) stores nothing, so you can retry it with the same key.

**Credits.** A generation with a live key costs 1 credit, charged when it is created (`creditsCharged`). If it fails, or you cancel it before it starts (`POST /generations/{id}/cancel`), the credit is refunded automatically (`creditsRefunded`). Without enough credits you get `402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` with `details.topUpUrl`; nothing is created. Live generations also count towards the concurrency and daily caps (see Rate limits).

**Test keys.** With an `ss_test_…` key everything works the same way (validation, uploads of the test environment, queue, statuses, idempotency, result URLs and delete), but no credits are used and no image model runs: the result is a sample image of exactly the requested size, and a missing caption becomes `Sample caption (test mode)`. Test generations do not count towards the generation caps.

**Results and retention.** Result URLs are signed and expire after 15 minutes (`result.urlsExpireAt`); `GET` the generation again for fresh ones. Results are kept until you `DELETE /generations/{id}` (results of test keys are deleted 30 days after they finish); a deleted generation keeps its record with `deletedAt` set. Input uploads expire after 30 days, so a generation queued from an expired upload fails with `UPLOAD_NOT_READY` and is refunded.

### Quick start
curl:
```sh
curl -s -X POST https://api.storeshot.art/v1/uploads -H "Authorization: Bearer $STORESHOT_API_KEY" -F file=@home.png
curl -s -X POST "https://api.storeshot.art/v1/generations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STORESHOT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Idempotency-Key: home-en-1" -H "Prefer: wait=60" \
  -d '{"inputs":[{"uploadId":"<upload id>"}],"store":"app_store","device":"app_store_1290x2796","app":{"name":"Trailmate"}}'
```
Node (18+, ES module):
```js
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
const api = 'https://api.storeshot.art/v1';
const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.STORESHOT_API_KEY}` };
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', new Blob([await readFile('home.png')]), 'home.png');
const upload = await (await fetch(`${api}/uploads`, { method: 'POST', headers, body: form })).json();
let gen = await (await fetch(`${api}/generations`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { ...headers, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Idempotency-Key': 'home-en-1' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ inputs: [{ uploadId: upload.id }], store: 'app_store', device: 'app_store_1290x2796', app: { name: 'Trailmate' } }),
})).json();
while (gen.status === 'queued' || gen.status === 'running') {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  gen = await (await fetch(`${api}/generations/${gen.id}`, { headers })).json();
}
console.log(gen.status, gen.result?.image.url ?? gen.error);
```
Python (requests):
```python
import os, time, requests
api, h = "https://api.storeshot.art/v1", {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['STORESHOT_API_KEY']}"}
upload = requests.post(f"{api}/uploads", headers=h, files={"file": open("home.png", "rb")}).json()
gen = requests.post(f"{api}/generations", headers={**h, "Idempotency-Key": "home-en-1", "Prefer": "wait=60"},
    json={"inputs": [{"uploadId": upload["id"]}], "store": "app_store", "device": "app_store_1290x2796", "app": {"name": "Trailmate"}}).json()
while gen["status"] in ("queued", "running"):
    time.sleep(3); gen = requests.get(f"{api}/generations/{gen['id']}", headers=h).json()
print(gen["status"], (gen["result"] or {}).get("image", {}).get("url") or gen["error"])
```

## Screenshot sets
`POST /screenshot-sets` turns 1–10 screenshots into a whole store listing in one call: every screen on every device of one or both stores, plus an optional Google Play feature graphic (`featureGraphic: true`), with one caption per screen and one palette and logo for all. Each image is a normal generation (listed by `GET /generations?screenshotSetId=<id>`), so statuses, refunds and test keys work exactly as above.

**Devices.** Without `devices`, a store gets the sizes its required screenshot groups ask for: the App Store `app_store_1290x2796` (6.9") and `app_store_1179x2556` (6.3"), Google Play `google_play_1080x1920`. Pass `devices` to choose fewer (or others, such as iPad or tablet sizes): only sizes that meet the store rules (`GET /stores/{store}/requirements`) are accepted, one per device class. A set has at most 50 images.

**Credits.** With a live key every image costs 1 credit, so a set costs `screens × devices (+1 for the feature graphic)`. Ask first with `?dryRun=true`: the quote (`images`, `credits`, `availableCredits`, `sufficient`) validates the request exactly like a create but creates and charges nothing. The create charges all images at once or none (`402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` with `details.requiredCredits`); the `202` response shows `creditsCharged`. A failed or canceled image is refunded; `POST /screenshot-sets/{id}/retry` creates new images for the failed ones only (1 credit each, again all or none). Repeating a retry never charges twice. A set counts as one generation towards the concurrency cap and all its images towards the daily cap.

**Status and download.** `GET /screenshot-sets/{id}` reports `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `partially_failed`, `failed` or `canceled`, with `counts` and every image. `GET /screenshot-sets/{id}/archive` streams a ZIP of the succeeded images plus `manifest.json` (`complete: false` lists what is missing): `<store>/<device>/<NN>.png`, or with `?layout=fastlane` the folders fastlane `deliver` (`fastlane/screenshots/en-US/`) and `supply` (`fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/`) read. `supply` replaces the images already in your Play listing.

### Quick start
curl:
```sh
curl -s -X POST "https://api.storeshot.art/v1/screenshot-sets?dryRun=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STORESHOT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @set.json
curl -s -X POST https://api.storeshot.art/v1/screenshot-sets -H "Authorization: Bearer $STORESHOT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Idempotency-Key: release-2.4" -d @set.json
curl -s -o listing.zip "https://api.storeshot.art/v1/screenshot-sets/<id>/archive?layout=fastlane" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STORESHOT_API_KEY"
```
with `set.json` `{"app":{"name":"Trailmate"},"screens":[{"input":{"uploadId":"<upload id>"},"caption":"Find every trail"}],"stores":[{"store":"app_store"},{"store":"google_play","featureGraphic":true}]}`.
Node (18+, ES module):
```js
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
const api = 'https://api.storeshot.art/v1';
const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.STORESHOT_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
const body = JSON.stringify({ app: { name: 'Trailmate' }, screens: [{ input: { uploadId: process.env.UPLOAD_ID }, caption: 'Find every trail' }], stores: [{ store: 'app_store' }] });
const quote = await (await fetch(`${api}/screenshot-sets?dryRun=true`, { method: 'POST', headers, body })).json();
console.log(`${quote.images} images, ${quote.credits} credits`);
let set = await (await fetch(`${api}/screenshot-sets`, { method: 'POST', headers: { ...headers, 'Idempotency-Key': 'release-2.4' }, body })).json();
while (set.status === 'queued' || set.status === 'running') {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000));
  set = await (await fetch(`${api}/screenshot-sets/${set.id}`, { headers })).json();
}
const zip = await fetch(`${api}/screenshot-sets/${set.id}/archive`, { headers });
await writeFile('listing.zip', Buffer.from(await zip.arrayBuffer()));
```
Python (requests):
```python
import os, time, requests
api, h = "https://api.storeshot.art/v1", {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['STORESHOT_API_KEY']}"}
body = {"app": {"name": "Trailmate"}, "screens": [{"input": {"uploadId": os.environ["UPLOAD_ID"]}, "caption": "Find every trail"}], "stores": [{"store": "app_store"}]}
print(requests.post(f"{api}/screenshot-sets", params={"dryRun": "true"}, headers=h, json=body).json()["credits"])
s = requests.post(f"{api}/screenshot-sets", headers={**h, "Idempotency-Key": "release-2.4"}, json=body).json()
while s["status"] in ("queued", "running"):
    time.sleep(5); s = requests.get(f"{api}/screenshot-sets/{s['id']}", headers=h).json()
open("listing.zip", "wb").write(requests.get(f"{api}/screenshot-sets/{s['id']}/archive", headers=h).content)
```

## Webhooks
Instead of polling, register an `https://` endpoint with `POST /webhooks` (scope `webhooks:write`, not granted by default) and receive a signed `POST` when a generation finishes (`generation.succeeded`, `generation.failed` incl. canceled), a screenshot set finishes (`screenshot_set.completed`) or the live balance falls below `creditsLowThreshold` (`credits.low`). A webhook belongs to one environment: test-key generations and sets reach test webhooks only. `POST /webhooks/{id}/test` sends a `webhook.test` event; `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` shows every attempt. The event bodies are documented under `webhooks` in this document.

**Delivery.** At least once, unordered, from `StoreshotWebhooks/1.0`. Any 2xx within 10 seconds acknowledges; redirects are not followed. Failures are retried after about 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h and 12 h (8 attempts, ~23 h), then the delivery is `exhausted`. Destinations must stay public: every attempt resolves the host again and refuses private addresses. Deduplicate on `Storeshot-Event-Id`. Generation payloads carry no download URLs: `GET /generations/{id}` for fresh ones.

**Signatures.** `Storeshot-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where `v1` = HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<t>.<raw body>`). Compute it over the exact bytes received, compare in constant time, accept any `v1` (two during a secret rotation grace) and reject a `t` more than 5 minutes away. The secret (`whsec_…`) is shown only by create and `POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`. Verification code for Node and Python: `docs/api/webhooks.md`.

**Limits.** 10 webhooks per environment, 10 test events per webhook per hour. URLs are shown masked (`https://<host>/…<last 4 path characters>`); delivery logs are kept 30 days.

## Billing
Buy one-time credit packs: `GET /billing/packs` lists them (empty while web payments are switched off), `POST /billing/checkout` with a `pack` returns a hosted checkout `url` for the buyer, and `GET /billing/checkouts/{id}` reports `open`, `processing`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `expired` or `failed`. Purchased credits are added once the payment succeeds and never expire; the payment provider is the merchant of record and applies taxes at checkout. A refund takes back the refunded share of the credits as far as they are unused. Scopes `billing:read` and `billing:write` are not granted by default; checkouts need a live credential. At most 10 checkouts per account per hour.

## Helpers
Free building blocks for agents (no credits; counted by the request rate limits only). `POST /palettes` extracts a brand palette from an upload or an `https://` URL with the same local algorithm as the Storeshot app (`extract`), or the dominant colour of up to 10 images (`dominant`); no AI model is involved and URL inputs are never stored. `GET /stores` and `GET /stores/{store}/requirements` describe what the App Store and Google Play need (formats, counts, sizes or dimension rules, required classes, the feature graphic), with the official pages they come from and which `GET /devices` sizes meet them.

scope.description: Space-separated scopes for the new key. Default `generations:write generations:read uploads:write usage:read`. `keys:manage`, `billing:write` and `webhooks:write` cannot be requested. The human may narrow the list, or add `billing:read` and `webhooks:read`.

No authentication. Send `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` and the `device_code` from `POST /auth/device`, as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (RFC 8628 §3.4) or JSON. **When to use.** Every `interval` seconds after `POST /auth/device`, until it returns the key; add 5 s on `slow_down`; stop on `access_denied` or `expired_token`.

**Credits.** Free: no credits.

Requires `generations:write`. Turns one screenshot into one store-ready marketing image of exactly the requested size. Requires `generations:write`. Turns 1–10 screenshots into a full store listing: every screen on every requested (or default) device of one or both stores, plus an optional Google Play feature graphic, with one caption per screen and one palette and logo for all. Each image is one generation (`GET /generations?screenshotSetId=`) and costs 1 credit with a live key: the whole set is created and charged at once, or nothing is (`402` with `details.requiredCredits`). Failed images are refunded; retry them with `POST /screenshot-sets/{id}/retry`. Test keys are free. `?dryRun=true` validates the same way and answers `200` with a quote (images and credits) without creating or charging anything. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried request never creates (or charges) twice.

**When to use.** For a store listing: every screen on every device of one or both stores in one call. Quote it first with `?dryRun=true`, then create it with an `Idempotency-Key` and poll `GET /screenshot-sets/{id}`.

**Credits.** 1 credit per image with a live key (screens × devices, +1 for a feature graphic), all charged at create or none (`402`); `?dryRun=true` quotes for free. Failed or canceled images are refunded; free with a test key (`ss_test_…`).

Requires `generations:write` and a credential of the set’s environment. Creates a new image (attempt + 1, at most 5 per slot) for every failed or canceled image, or for the given `generationIds`, at 1 credit each with a live key, all at once or none (`402`). Images that are superseded, still running or succeeded are skipped (`retry.skipped`); if nothing is left to retry the answer is `409 SCREENSHOT_SET_STATE_CONFLICT` and nothing is charged, so repeating a retry never charges twice.

**When to use.** After a set ends `partially_failed` or `failed`, to make new images for the failed slots only.

**Credits.** 1 credit per new image with a live key, all or none (`402`); nothing when there is nothing to retry (`409`); free with a test key (`ss_test_…`).

get.description:
Requires `generations:read` or `generations:write`. Streams a ZIP of every succeeded image (the current attempt of each slot) and a `manifest.json` listing the files and the missing images. `layout=store` (default): `<store>/<device>/<NN>.<ext>`. `layout=fastlane`: `fastlane/screenshots/en-US/<NN>_<device>.png` for `deliver` and `fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/{phoneScreenshots,sevenInchScreenshots,tenInchScreenshots}/<NN>.png` + `featureGraphic.jpg` for `supply` (note: `supply` replaces the images already in your listing). `409 SCREENSHOT_SET_STATE_CONFLICT` when no image has succeeded yet; `503` with `Retry-After` when the server is busy building other archives.

**When to use.** Once the set is final, to save every image: `?layout=fastlane` for the fastlane folders, or the default `<store>/<device>/<NN>.png` layout.

**Credits.** Free: no credits.
